mutation.description: the dash-glued dot-lost deepseek-v3-1 is variant-pinned to v3.1 so it merges into the dotted deepseek/v3.1 entity instead of minting a phantom deepseek@1

provenance.ref: deepseek encodes its point release as a VARIANT token (deepseek-v3.1 -> deepseek/v3.1), so the dash-glued deepseek-v3-1 lost the dot and minted a phantom deepseek@1; an exact-id idFamilyOverride pins variant v3.1, converging it onto deepseek/v3.1 (14 serving instances). DeepSeek-V3.1 is a real release: https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250929

mutation.description: the org-prefixed dash-glued deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V3-1 is variant-pinned to v3.1 so it converges onto deepseek/v3.1 alongside the bare dashed and dotted spellings

provenance.ref: org-prefixed spelling of the same DeepSeek-V3.1 model (togetherai); a distinct idFamilyOverride key (the lookup is exact-id) pinning variant v3.1 onto the served entity deepseek/v3.1. https://api-docs.deepseek.com/news/news250929

mutation.description: translate is now a peeled identity modifier so Command A Translate keys as command/a{translate}, a distinct entity that stops collapsing onto (and overwriting the metadata of) base command/a

provenance.ref: Cohere ships Command A Translate as a DISTINCT model from base Command A (https://docs.cohere.com/docs/command-a-translate); adding 'translate' to modifiers.json (identity by default class) peels it so the served command-a-translate-08-2025 keys as command/a{translate} rather than the coarse command/a it previously collapsed onto
